items.title: The Pirate Queen Who Ruled The South China Sea
items.author: Weird History
items.content:
<article>The world's most successful pirate wasn't Blackbeard. In fact, it wasn't even a man. While most pirate captains struggled to command a single ship, one legendary woman built a fleet of nearly 2,000 ships and led an astonishing 80,000 sailors, creating one of the most powerful pirate empires in history. 

On this episode of Weird History we take a look at the life of Pirate Queen Zheng Yi Sao. How did she rise from obscurity to dominate the seas? And why have so few people heard of the pirate many historians consider the greatest pirate of all time?

Have you heard the tales of the Pirate Queen? Let us know in the comments!

items.title: The Strange Story of America’s First “Alien Abduction”
items.author: Weird History
items.content:
<article>During a late-night drive through rural New Hampshire in 1961, Barney and Betty Hill reported a terrifying encounter with a UFO that would change their lives forever. Since then, their story remains one of the most famous and controversial alien abduction cases in history. From unexplained missing time and hypnotic regression to eerie eyewitness testimony, the Hills' account helped shape modern beliefs about extraterrestrials, UFO sightings, and even the mysteries surrounding Area 51. But were they telling the truth, or did something else happen that night?

In this episode of Weird History Presents: Graveyard Shift, we explore the shocking details behind America's first widely publicized alien abduction case, the evidence that still fuels debate decades later, and why the Barney and Betty Hill story continues to captivate believers and skeptics alike.

Do you think it's possible that the Hills were really abducted by aliens? Let us know in the comments!

Be sure to subscribe to the Weird History Newsletter: https://bit.ly/WeirdHistoryNews


#uap #alienabduction #weirdhistory</article>

items.title: The End Of America’s Most Dangerous Amusement Park | Last Days
items.author: Weird History
items.content:
<article>New Jersey's Action Park, the world's most infamous water park, closed its doors in 1996. It eventually reopened as Mountain Creek Waterpark, but in 2014 the son of the original owner brought back the legendary Action Park name. His goal was simple: recreate the thrill that made the original park famous, just without the injuries, lawsuits, and deadly reputation. But reviving America's most dangerous amusement park proved far more complicated than anyone expected.

LAST DAYS is Weird History’s prestige format series focusing on final chapters, deaths, downfalls and conclusions. In this episode, we examine the shocking true story behind Action Park's controversial comeback, the accidents that defined its legacy, and why the park's final chapter ended in failure.

items.title: «Главные теории физики НЕ ДОКАЗАНЫ» — Сабина Хоссенфельдер про устройство Вселенной
items.content:
Правда ли, что скорость света — не абсолютный предел, путешествия во времени могут оказаться возможными, а некоторые из самых популярных теорий современной физики вообще невозможно проверить?

В новом выпуске — разговор с Сабиной Хоссенфельдер, физиком-теоретиком, доктором наук и одним из самых известных научных популяризаторов в мире. Мы обсудили главные загадки современной физики: происхождение Вселенной, природу времени, возможность существования внеземных цивилизаций, искусственный интеллект, свободу воли и теории, которые сегодня вызывают больше всего споров среди ученых.

— Почему скорость света может быть не пределом для передачи информации?

— Почему человечество может искать инопланетные цивилизации совершенно не там?

— Возможны ли путешествия во времени с точки зрения современной физики?

— Почему свобода воли может оказаться иллюзией?

— Может ли искусственный интеллект когда-нибудь стать по-настоящему разумным?

— Живем ли мы внутри компьютерной симуляции?

— Почему мультивселенную невозможно доказать?

— Что на самом деле известно о Большом взрыве и первом моменте существования Вселенной?

— Почему Сабина считает многие современные космологические теории скорее математическими историями, чем наукой?

items.title: The chemotherapy-induced senescence-associated secretome promotes cell detachment and metastatic dissemination through metabolic reprogramming
items.author: Katherine M. Aird
items.content: Cole and colleagues identify fructose as a component of the secretome in therapy-induced senescent ovarian cancer cells that drives metastasis. Fructose metabolically reprograms neighboring cancer cells, enhancing their ability to detach by reducing plasma membrane cholesterol through modulation of complex I and NAD.

items.title: Agentic AI for scaling diagnosis and care in neurodegenerative disease
items.author: Pedro Pinheiro-Chagas
items.content: In this Perspective, the authors envision that agentic AI systems may in the future support clinical workflows for neurodegenerative disease diagnosis and care. They propose a system for scaling specialist-level dementia care via synergistic collaborations between humans and an AI-driven continuously learning healthcare system that can reason across all patient data.

items.title: Plasma proteomics framework predicts metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease up to 16 years before onset
items.author: Hao Chen
items.content: Using plasma proteomics, Yu, Chen, Feng, Li et. al report a panel of five blood proteins that can predict future risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) up to 16 years before clinical onset, offering a potential tool for early risk stratification.

items.title: Ultra-early proteomic signatures predict MASLD up to 16 years ahead
items.content: A plasma proteomic signature enables accurate prediction of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) up to 16 years before diagnosis, and offers a clinically applicable proteomic framework for early risk stratification and preventive intervention.

items.content:

items.title: Why The Most Dangerous Men Were Terrifed Of Griselda Blanco

items.content:
<article>Most people picture gangsters as powerful men in sharp suits, surrounded by cigar smoke, luxury, and violence. But one of the most feared crime bosses in history was a woman… and she was so ruthless that even Pablo Escobar was afraid of her.
